Paraphrase of the page: 'In 988, Oliba entered Montecassino and left Besalú [...] to Bernard Tallaferro'. The Oliba Cabreta page has no dated sentence for the division but says Bernard received Besalú and Ripoll, Wilfred Cerdanya, and Oliba Berga; the Berga page: 'The town later had its own counts from 988.'

ledger.note: 988: Vallespir, Fenouillèdes and Peyrepertuse go with Besalú to Bernard Tallaferro. Paraphrase of the page: Oliba 'left Besalú, along with Vallespir, Fenouillèdes, and Peyrepertuse, to Bernard Tallaferro'.

1002: Berga, which had its own counts from 988, is annexed to Cerdanya and the one row goes on as Cerdanya. 'In 1002, Berga was annexed to Cerdanya.' The state, colour and dossier continue (Cliopatria's row follows Cerdanya-Berga before and after); the 1003 outline grows by 597 km2.
1002: Ripoll passes to Besalú. Paraphrase of the page: Bernard Tallaferro 'annexed Ripoll in 1002'; the Oliba Cabreta page puts Ripoll in his share in 988.

1111: Vallespir, Fenolledès, Peyrepertuse and Castellnou come to Cerdanya as compensation for Barcelona's inheritance of Besalú. Paraphrase of the page: the dispute with 'Bernard William of Cerdanya, Besalú's feudal suzerain' was settled when they 'were ceded to Cerdanya as compensation'. The page does not date the settlement; 1111 is the inheritance year.

region.text: Cerdanya, Berga and the trans-Pyrenean districts

ledger.note: 1117: Cerdanya passes to Ramon Berenguer III of Barcelona. 'He inherited the counties of Besalú (1111) and Cerdanya (1117)'. The Cerdanya page: 'In 1118, Cerdanya was sold to Barcelona' (count list: Raymond Berengar I from 1118). Cliopatria's Barcelona shape takes the land over in 1126.

1162: Cerdanya passes from Barcelona to Peter, a younger son of Ramon Berenguer IV, and is a county of its own again. The Cerdanya page lists 'Peter (1162–1168)'; the Ramon Berenguer IV page: 'Pere (Peter) received Cerdanya and lands north of the Pyrenees' (undated; the count died on 6 August 1162). Cliopatria resumes the row in 1169.
1168: Sancho I succeeds as count of Cerdanya. The Cerdanya page lists 'Sancho I (1168–1223)'; the Alfonso II page: 'the counties of Cerdanya (1168) and Roussillon (inherited in 1172)'.

1199: Berga is sold to King Peter II of Aragon. 'Berga was sold to king Peter II of Aragon in 1199.' The page is about the town and does not say what the count of Cerdanya kept; Sancho I is listed as count of Cerdanya until 1223.

region.text: the county of Roussillon (with Conflent, Vallespir and the Fenouillèdes edge)

ledger.note: About 1209: Peter II of Aragon grants Roussillon to his uncle Sancho, who now holds Cerdanya and Roussillon together. 'King Peter II of Aragon granted around 1209 to his uncle Sancho the county of Roussillon'; Roussillon had passed to Alfonso II in 1172 ('Annexed into the Principality of Catalonia: 1172'). Cliopatria enlarges the row in 1188.
1223: Nuño Sánchez succeeds Sancho I. The Cerdanya page lists 'Nuño (1223–1242)'; the Roussillon page: 'Sancho I of Roussillon-Cerdanya, was succeeded by his son Nuño Sánchez'.
1242: Nuño Sánchez dies and Cerdanya and Roussillon revert to the Crown of Aragon. 'Nuño Sánchez, on whose death in 1242, his Counties reverted to the Crown of Aragon.' Cliopatria's row ends in 1235.
1242: the appanage of Cerdanya and Roussillon ends and its land goes to the Crown of Aragon.

notes: WHAT THIS ROW IS. The Berga page is the town's: it never names a County of Berga. By the pages the Berguedà was a pagus of Cerdanya, had its own counts only from 988 (the Berga page, the Oliba Cabreta page) and was 'annexed to Cerdanya' in 1002. Cliopatria's 'County of Berga' row (898-1235) is the Cerdanya-Berga complex throughout: its 898 polygon (19 grid cells) holds Berga, Puigcerdà, Llívia, Ripoll, Solsona and Cardona. The dossier therefore treats the row as the County of Cerdanya under Berga's label; a county-of-cerdanya dossier (798-1403 on the Cerdanya page) is listed as a counterpart that needs one; the 1002 annexation of Berga to Cerdanya is written as a rename of this row, not as a merger. CLIOPATRIA GAPS. 960-989 (the union is drawn in the Besalú row), 1028-1039 (the Ribagorza row covers it), 1126-1168 (Barcelona's shape covers it) and 1236-1242 (the row stops in 1235) are covered by new keyframes or by the Barcelona dossier. The Cliopatria steps 1040, 1056, 1085, 1094, 1099, 1177 and 1210-1227 cannot be explained by any page opened (verdict ok, unverified). UNSETTLED. (a) 1117 (Ramon Berenguer III page) or 1118 (Cerdanya page) for the sale to Barcelona; 1117 is used. (b) Whether the 1199 sale of Berga took the Berguedà out of Sancho I's county: the page is about the town; the loss is recorded at confidence 2 and the 1199-1242 outlines are not cut, so the renderer will apply the event on top of them. (c) The 1188 enlargement of the Cliopatria outline against the c. 1209 grant of Roussillon (Roussillon page). (d) The Berga page's infobox has an 'Area' label for the town and comarca; the fetch returned no figure, and it is not the county's area, so no infobox comparison was made. NOT OPENED: the County of Cerdanya page was read for Berga, Besalú and Oliba; no page for Conflent, Capcir or the Cerdanya counts' seat (Llívia or Puigcerdà). Gazetteer names needed: Berga, Ripoll, Vic (places); Cerdanya, Berguedà, Conflent, Vallespir, Fenouillèdes, Peyrepertuse (regions or places). Circles by coordinates stand in.
